findings.title: Re-approval of a changed dependency silently revives stale consumers
findings.expected: Consumer review stays stale after an input changes, even when that input is independently re-approved.
findings.observed: Original checker validates current per-file records and names only; both negative reproductions fail with Missing expected exception.
findings.repair: Schema-2 exact review-time source-input map for transitive dependencies plus governance; check each reachable record and bind full key set; per-invocation digest cache only.
findings.preserved: Existing public methods/results, cycle handling, status/date/evidence validation and read-only bootstrap.
tests: refreshed dependency must not revive its stale consumer
refreshed governance must invalidate consumer snapshots
transitive refresh does not revive a grandparent consumer
consumer and dependency re-audit restores usable fixture

findings.title: Registry is not bound to the canonical installation worktree
findings.expected: A registry declared for another worktree cannot authenticate this installation.
findings.observed: Original loadRegistry ignores the wrong worktree value; negative test fails with Missing expected exception.
findings.repair: Require schema 2, configured context and exact realpath worktree; ship null worktree/UNCONFIGURED and document evidence-backed migration.
findings.preserved: No auto-approval or new permissions. Worktree relocation deliberately invalidates trust, not public skill contracts.
findings.limitation: Same-path replacement, branch/task changes and external runtime changes still need reviewer-managed context invalidation.
tests: copied approval must not authenticate another worktree
schema 1 approval requires explicit re-audit, not promotion

findings.observed: Before inventory has 122 paths and excludes those namespaces; after has 229 deduplicated paths.

findings.preserved: Read-only inventory and explicit NOT_SEMANTIC_APPROVAL status; no automatic dependency discovery claimed.
findings.limitation: Actual external/global resolution and referenced root/project resources require review beyond this inventory.

findings.severity: HIGH (conditional exposure of local readable checkpoint targets)
findings.title: Session checkpoint helpers follow symlinks and read unbounded raw state

sources.quoted_source:
# --- Active session state recovery ---
STATE_FILE="production/session-state/active.md"
if [ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "=== ACTIVE SESSION STATE DETECTED ==="
    echo "A previous session left state at: $STATE_FILE"
    echo "Inspect this checkpoint and verify its revision, scope and unresolved work before resuming."
    echo ""
    echo "Quick summary:"
    head -20 "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null
    TOTAL_LINES=$(wc -l < "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$TOTAL_LINES" -gt 20 ]; then
        echo "  ... ($TOTAL_LINES total lines — read the full file to continue)"
    fi

# --- Active session state file ---
STATE_FILE="production/session-state/active.md"
if [ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "## Active Session State (from $STATE_FILE)"
    STATE_LINES=$(wc -l < "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
    if [ "$STATE_LINES" -gt 100 ] 2>/dev/null; then
        head -n 100 "$STATE_FILE"
        echo "... (truncated — $STATE_LINES total lines, showing first 100)"
    else
        cat "$STATE_FILE"
    fi
else
    echo ""
    echo "## No active session state file found"
    echo "Consider maintaining production/session-state/active.md for better recovery."
fi

# --- Snapshot state; session exit is NOT proof of task completion ---
STATE_FILE="production/session-state/active.md"
if [ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]; then
    # Copy to the log without deleting the durable recovery checkpoint.
    {
        echo "## Archived Session State: $TIMESTAMP"
        cat "$STATE_FILE"
        echo "---"
        echo ""
    } >> "$SESSION_LOG_DIR/session-log.md" || { echo "ERROR: session log write failed; recovery state retained" >&2; exit 2; }
    # Keep active.md even when logging fails; unresolved work must survive.

findings.expected: A checkpoint symlink must not expose or archive an unintended file; unsafe data/type/size should fail safely and preserve state.
findings.observed: Disposable private canary is printed by start/compact and archived by stop. Original line limits do not bound bytes, and raw reads repeat the path.
findings.repair: Reuse one bounded regular UTF-8 checkpoint reader with component symlink checks, no-follow/nonblocking open where supported, read/fstat guards and ASCII-control rejection. Reuse snapshot, deny special log files, restrictive umask.
findings.preserved: Valid checkpoint previews/archives and incomplete active.md retained; existing logging errors still reported.
findings.limitation: No secret redaction or hostile-filesystem race resistance claimed. FIFO/size/control variants have final regressions; only symlink exposure was executed in the original red suite.

findings.title: Git inspection failure is reported as a clean worktree

sources.quoted_source:
CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only 2>/dev/null)
STAGED=$(git diff --staged --name-only 2>/dev/null)
UNTRACKED=$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard 2>/dev/null)

if [ -n "$CHANGED" ]; then
    echo "Unstaged changes:"
    echo "$CHANGED" | while read -r f; do echo "  - $f"; done
fi
if [ -n "$STAGED" ]; then
    echo "Staged changes:"
    echo "$STAGED" | while read -r f; do echo "  - $f"; done
fi
if [ -n "$UNTRACKED" ]; then
    echo "New untracked files:"
    echo "$UNTRACKED" | while read -r f; do echo "  - $f"; done
fi
if [ -z "$CHANGED" ] && [ -z "$STAGED" ] && [ -z "$UNTRACKED" ]; then
    echo "  (no uncommitted changes)"

findings.expected: Cleanliness cannot be asserted when Git inspection fails.
findings.observed: Removing .git from a disposable test repo leads to (no uncommitted changes); original negative assertion fails.
findings.repair: Track inspection command success and output UNVERIFIED on any failure; only emit clean if successful checks are empty.
findings.preserved: Advisory nature of compaction helper, changed-file summaries, checkpoint retention and requested logging.
